justification: Abstract's object is verifiers (step checkers, proof assistants) and what their verdicts guarantee; it proposes VAL as a meta-standard resolving conflation across 17 surveyed papers, i.e. a taxonomy of the field.

Contribution is a security-aware agent atop an information-flow-control defense that provably blocks unsafe actions and reduces HITL approvals; evaluated only in the lab on the AgentDojo and WASP benchmarks.

Abstract targets runtime oversight that decides whether to intervene rather than let the agent continue, replacing scalar risk gating with intervention advantage; measured in the lab across four benchmarks including ALFWorld.

Design principle is 'autonomy at decision points, not over pipelines', confining decisions to bounded typed surfaces inside pre-committed pipelines; reported from a 78-day deployment across three live Tencent business lines.

Six interaction mechanisms (co-planning, action guards, approval before acting) decide whether the loop may proceed unaided; the prototype is studied in the lab via simulated user testing and qualitative studies, not in deployment.

Contribution is an instrument, not a loop mechanism: orchestration code scored against an autonomy taxonomy (impact, oversight); it is only demonstrated on AutoGen and select applications, with no full validation.

GAIE's OCM is a deterministic decision function routing code-generation tasks to oversight tiers before release; the framework is argued and mapped to regulations with analytical modeling rather than empirically validated.

Framework separates allowed from capable autonomy, i.e. what an agent is authorized to execute given oversight and reversibility; it structures the field as autonomy levels and only illustrates via one enterprise agent.

Object is the approval gate's escalation policy deciding which agent actions stop for a human; evidence is a lab set of 125 hand-labeled actions plus fatigue modeling, with the authors noting a human study is only motivated.

Compares four oversight strategies governing whether computer-use agent actions proceed or are interrupted; evidence is a lab mixed-methods study with 48 participants in a live web environment, not a deployed setting.
LLM A* shapes the A* search space with LLM commonsense and human feedback, claiming fewer expanded states; validated in the lab by comparative analysis against A* and RL baselines.

Contribution is an auditing instrument (blind-spot mass, oversight-cost identity) for measuring where autonomy is statistically supported; instantiated in the lab on the public BPIC 2019 log with a simulated agent.

Artifacts specify the delegated-autonomy boundary: graduated authority, oversight and how control is returned before an agent may act; proposed and only illustrated with two contrasting example agents.
Object is monitors detecting covert agent misbehavior plus a new hybrid monitor scaffolding, an audit of one named mechanism; stress tests run in the lab on SHADE-Arena and CUA-SHADE-Arena.
Replaces LLM-as-a-Judge with Dafny/Z3 proof of compiled constraints, i.e. the judgement that gates agent behavior; validated in the lab across three benchmarks and seven agent models.

Specialized gates diagnose failure modes and recommend loopbacks, with human checkpoints holding authority; evaluated in the lab on five matched economic-theory tasks against an ungated baseline with blinded evaluators.

Contribution is a constraint substrate (access control, network policy, enforced conventions) bounding what a coding agent may do and making review tractable; evidence is a controlled experiment with 11 inserted backdoors.

Automated checks flag readability, fidelity and accessibility risk and escalate to mandatory HITL review before release; the oversight-by-design approach is proposed and argued with no evaluation reported.
Headline artefact is an instrument, a benchmark and ASD metric for comparing scalable-oversight protocols; evidence is one demonstrative experiment benchmarking Debate rather than a full validation.

STARS widens the LLM response space and evaluates, repairs and selects among candidate responses; lab experiments vary oversight condition, reporting 77-94% task completion without and 100% with human confirmation.

TAO's contribution is the arrangement itself: a hierarchical tier structure routing tasks by complexity with inter- and intra-tier communication; validated in the lab on five healthcare safety benchmarks plus ablations.

Framework is about coordination and communication among heterogeneous human and computational agents (MAS versus Centaurian, communication-space layers, Petri nets), a conceptual structuring of the field with no evaluation.

HiLSVA's claim is explicit human oversight and handoff deciding whether the agent proceeds in a mixed-initiative workflow; evidence is lab case studies and a controlled user study with twelve participants.

AMAOS gates task execution through HITL verification checkpoints, risk scoring and conditional human-approval edges in the agent DAG; evidence is three enterprise case studies with no reported production deployment.

Specialized gates diagnose failure modes and recommend loopbacks, with human checkpoints holding authority; evaluated in the lab on five matched economic-theory tasks against an ungated baseline with blinded evaluators.
